Anyquery is a SQL query engine that allows you to run SQL queries on pretty much anything. It supports querying files, databases, and apps (e.g. Apple Notes, Notion, Chrome, Todoist, etc.). It's built on top of SQLite and uses plugins to extend its functionality.
It can also connect to LLMs (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, TypingMind, etc.) to allow them to access your data.
Finally, it can act as a MySQL server, allowing you to run SQL queries from your favorite MySQL-compatible client (e.g. TablePlus, Metabase, etc.).

You can also connect to clients that supports function calling (e.g. ChatGPT, TypingMind). Refer to each connection guide in the documentation for more information.
The documentation provides detailed instructions on how to run queries with Anyquery.

The documentation provides detailed instructions on how to install Anyquery on your system. You can install anyquery from Homebrew, APT, YUM/DNF, Scoop, Winget and Chocolatey. You can also download the binary from the releases page.
Anyquery is plugin-based, and you can install plugins to extend its functionality. You can install plugins from the official registry or create your own. Anyquery can also load any SQLite extension.
Anyquery is built and maintained by one person. Sponsoring keeps it free and open-source, and puts your logo in this README and on anyquery.dev.

This is a sample application demonstrating Quarkus features and best practices. The application allows superheroes to fight against supervillains. The application consists of several microservices, communicating either synchronously via REST or asynchronously using Kafka. All the data used by the applications are on the `characterdata` branch of this repository.
- Super Hero Battle UI - A React application served via Quarkus Quinoa
- Villain REST API - A classical HTTP microservice with Hibernate ORM with Panache (active record pattern)
- Hero REST API - A reactive HTTP microservice with Hibernate Reactive with Panache (repository pattern)
- Narration REST API - A blocking HTTP microservice integrating with OpenAI via LangChain4J
- Location gRPC API - A Kotlin gRPC microservice with Hibernate ORM with Panache
- Fight REST API - A reactive HTTP microservice orchestrating fights, using MongoDB, Kafka, and resilience patterns
- Event Statistics - An event-driven microservice consuming Kafka events and serving statistics via WebSockets
- Grafana LGTM Stack - All services export traces, metrics, and logs via OpenTelemetry (OTLP)

1. Create an empty private repo on GitHub, or anywhere git can push.
|`kanzo`|Starts the board at http://localhost:4242 and opens it; `--port` for another port, `--no-open` to not open it|
|`kanzo service install`|Keeps the board running and starts it at login; `uninstall` removes it|
|`kanzo mcp`|The MCP server for agents: they start it, not you|
|`kanzo share on`|Shares the board with the other computers on your network; `off` stops, while the board keeps running|
|`kanzo join <ip>`|Uses the board another computer shares, from this one's board and agents; `kanzo leave` goes back|
|`kanzo sync`|Commits the board and pulls or pushes it; `--repo <url>` sets the repo, `--keep-local` or `--keep-remote` when both sides changed|
|`kanzo export`|Prints the board as Markdown; `-f json` for JSON, `-p <project>` for one project, `-o <file>` to save it|
|`kanzo update`|Installs the latest release and restarts the board's service; the board offers new versions too|
|`kanzo init`|Creates the data folder; the first run does this too|
|Board of 3,000 tasks|17 ms to load in the browser|
|Agents' tool list|about 1,000 tokens, once per session|
|Agents' replies|10 to 60 tokens of plain text|
